I found exactly how it works. The CLI has a hidden `--cloud-url` flag that overrides the default base URL (`https://cloud.specstory.com`, set in [sync.go:615](specstory-cli/pkg/cloud/sync.go:615)).

## How to point the CLI at local cloud

Pass `--cloud-url http://localhost:5173` to any cloud-aware command. It's wired into `login`, `logout`, `sync`, `run`, and `watch` ([main.go:1474-1492](specstory-cli/main.go:1474), [login.go:211](specstory-cli/pkg/cmd/login.go:211)). It's a hidden flag, so it won't show in `--help`, but it works.

The flag feeds `cloud.SetAPIBaseURL()` in `PersistentPreRunE` ([main.go:213](specstory-cli/main.go:213)), and the cloud package then builds endpoints like `<base>/api/v1/device-login`, `<base>/cli-login`, etc. against it.

**Typical workflow:**

```zsh
# 1. Authenticate against your local cloud (opens <base>/cli-login)
specstory login --cloud-url http://localhost:5173

# 2. Run live capture against local cloud
specstory run --cloud-url http://localhost:5173

# or one-shot sync of existing sessions
specstory sync --cloud-url http://localhost:5173
```

You must pass `--cloud-url` on **every** invocation (login included) — it's a per-process flag, not persisted. The auth token you get from logging in against localhost is stored separately from a prod token, but since the flag isn't sticky, always include it so you don't accidentally hit prod.

**Two related hidden flags** you may find handy with a local backend:
- `--cloud-token <refresh-token>` — bypass interactive login for a session ([main.go:1463](specstory-cli/main.go:1463))
- `--debug` / `--log` — see the actual HTTP calls to confirm it's hitting `localhost:5173`

One thing to confirm on your end: your local cloud serves the device-auth endpoints (`/api/v1/device-login`, `/api/v1/device-refresh`, `/cli-login`) on `5173`, since that's what the CLI will call.
